facts.fact: Pandas is the primary Python library for data manipulation and analysis
A DataFrame is a 2D labeled data structure with columns of potentially different types
df.head() shows the first 5 rows, df.tail() shows the last 5 rows
df.describe() generates descriptive statistics for numeric columns
df.info() shows column types, non-null counts, and memory usage
df.groupby() splits data into groups for aggregation and transformation
df.merge() combines DataFrames like SQL JOINs on specified columns
df.pivot_table() creates spreadsheet-style pivot tables with aggregation
df.fillna() replaces missing values with a specified value or method
df.dropna() removes rows or columns containing missing values
df.sort_values() sorts by one or more columns in ascending or descending order
df.apply() applies a function along an axis of the DataFrame
pd.read_csv() reads CSV files into DataFrames with automatic type inference
pd.to_datetime() converts strings or numbers to datetime objects
df.resample() groups time series data by time frequency for aggregation
NumPy provides the ndarray — a fast multidimensional array object
np.mean(), np.median(), np.std() compute basic statistics on arrays
np.where() returns elements chosen from arrays based on a condition
Matplotlib is the foundational Python plotting library
Seaborn builds on Matplotlib with higher-level statistical visualizations
SELECT retrieves data from one or more tables
WHERE filters rows based on conditions before grouping
GROUP BY groups rows sharing a value so aggregate functions can be applied
HAVING filters groups after aggregation — like WHERE but for grouped data
JOIN combines rows from two or more tables based on a related column
INNER JOIN returns rows when there is a match in both tables
LEFT JOIN returns all rows from the left table and matched rows from the right
RIGHT JOIN returns all rows from the right table and matched rows from the left
FULL OUTER JOIN returns rows when there is a match in either table
UNION combines result sets of two or more SELECT statements (removes duplicates)
UNION ALL combines result sets without removing duplicates
Subqueries are queries nested inside another query — in SELECT, FROM, or WHERE
CTEs (Common Table Expressions) with WITH clause create temporary named result sets
Window functions (ROW_NUMBER, RANK, LAG, LEAD) operate on a set of rows related to the current row
OVER clause defines the window for window functions with PARTITION BY and ORDER BY
Indexes speed up data retrieval — CREATE INDEX on frequently queried columns
Primary keys uniquely identify each row in a table
Foreign keys establish relationships between tables and enforce referential integrity
Normalization reduces data redundancy by organizing into related tables
EXPLAIN shows the query execution plan for performance analysis
Mean is the average — sum of values divided by count
Median is the middle value when data is sorted — robust to outliers
Mode is the most frequently occurring value
Standard deviation measures the spread of data around the mean
Variance is the average squared deviation from the mean
Correlation measures the strength and direction of a linear relationship between two variables
Pearson correlation ranges from -1 (perfect negative) to +1 (perfect positive)
P-value is the probability of observing results at least as extreme given the null hypothesis is true
Null hypothesis (H0) assumes no effect or no difference
Alternative hypothesis (H1) is what you want to prove
Type I error rejects a true null hypothesis (false positive)
Type II error fails to reject a false null hypothesis (false negative)
Confidence interval gives a range likely to contain the true population parameter
T-test compares means between two groups
ANOVA compares means across three or more groups
Chi-square test assesses relationships between categorical variables
Linear regression models the relationship between a dependent variable and one or more independent variables
R-squared measures how well the regression model explains the variance in the data
Normal distribution is symmetric bell-shaped — 68% within 1 SD, 95% within 2 SD
Central Limit Theorem: sample means approach normal distribution as sample size increases
Bar charts compare quantities across categories
Line charts show trends over time or continuous data
Scatter plots show relationships between two numeric variables
Histograms show the distribution of a single numeric variable
Box plots show median, quartiles, and outliers of a distribution
Heatmaps display matrix data with color intensity
Pie charts show proportions of a whole — use sparingly, bar charts are often better
Stacked bar charts show both total and composition across categories
Area charts are line charts with the area below filled — good for volume over time
Dual-axis charts combine two different scales on the same plot
Color should be meaningful and accessible — use colorblind-friendly palettes
Chart titles should describe what the viewer should take away
Axis labels must include units of measurement
Legends should be positioned where they don't obscure data
Gridlines should be subtle — they support reading, not dominate
Annotations call out specific data points or events
Dashboards combine multiple visualizations to tell a complete story
Interactivity (filters, drill-downs, tooltips) lets users explore data themselves
Tableau is a leading drag-and-drop visualization platform
Data storytelling combines visualization with narrative to drive decisions
